results.correct_value: 7 pitches counted from the treed ledge: P1 copperhead + six-bolt slab (5.11), P2 slab (5.10), P3 crack/roof (5.11), P4 corner (5.10), P5 crux thin slab (5.12a), P6-P7 hand/finger crack (5.9). The roped 5.8 block pitch is an approach option onto the ledge, not a route pitch.
results.evidence: The route's published pitch-by-pitch description numbers from the treed ledge: P1 cracks then slab past a fixed copperhead and six bolts (.11), P2 slab (.10), P3 crack/roof (.11), P4 corner (.10), P5 very thin slab crux (.12a), P6-7 hand and finger crack (.9); the 5.8 block is listed under Location as one way to reach the ledge. The first-ascent account in the 1990 AAJ calls it a seven-pitch route with the crux friction slab on the fifth pitch. So beta/rack/rappel table are right and pitch_detail was shifted by a prepended approach pitch; the pitch count (8) and every '8 pitches' copy were wrong too.

results.correct_value: This is Concord Tower's South Face (5.6, 3 pitches, Grade II, FA 1965), starting from the far eastern edge of the Concord-Lexington notch and finishing over the shark fin to Concord's summit. The row is filed on the wrong tower.
results.evidence: The identical beta (price-of-admission gravelly traverse, sandy spot by the shark fin, pink tricam on the summit block, bolts on the summit, rappel to the notch) and the 1965 Cramer/Anderson/Schuler/Stanley FA are listed under Concord Tower as its South Face; a second route database also lists South Face under Concord Tower with the same FA party and describes the shark fin finish. Settled by research, but the fix is re-filing the row to Concord Tower (area_id, name, summit waypoint), which is out of scope for text patches; patching prose alone would contradict the page's Lexington header.

results.evidence: USGS 1 m elevation at the stored pin is 5,151 ft (10 m DEM 5,138 ft), which supports ~5,100 ft over 5,450, and the pullout sits below Washington Pass (5,477 ft). But no published elevation for the pond pullout itself was found, and whether the pin sits exactly at the pond is not confirmed, so only one source.

Sources give only time (30-45 min, some parties about an hour), no mileage. The 'roughly a third of a mile' and 'several hundred feet' are suspect (the straight line from the pullout pin to the summit pin is ~0.65 mi and the wall base sits ~1,500 ft above the road), and the 6.5-mile day is a loop via the Blue Lake Trail and a highway walk, but no source publishes the one-way distance or gain.
